author: DTrim99
body:
Two things are going on, and neither is an eligibility problem — PE now grants the credit; the $0 you saw was the frozen-ceiling bug you reported on #1155 (PE was capping WFTC eligibility at the 2022 federal-EITC completed-phase-out income, $59,190 for 3 kids MFJ; your AGI $61,289 fell above it). That's fixed in PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9351 (merged 2026-09-01), and the current build behind this output shows the credit.

On the amount: your $561 uses a $0.24-per-dollar phase-out rate, which is the **2022** rate. WAC 458-20-285(10)(D) publishes $0.12/$0.12/$0.18/$0.24 for 0/1/2/3 children as "the 2022 tax year adjustments," and says the department "will adjust the WFTC refund reduction amounts on an annual basis beginning in 2023." Those rates are max ÷ phase-out band (1,200/5,000 = 0.24 in 2022); for 2023 the max uprates to $1,255, so the rate becomes 1,255/5,000 = 0.251 and the credit reaches zero exactly at the ceiling. That gives ≈ $529, a bit below your $561.

PE's current $558.70 is off from both because a separate open bug computes the rate as (max − $50)/band ≈ 0.241; the fix (PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9391) switches it to max/band, landing at ≈$529. I'll ping you when that merges.
